voices.note: R' Yehuda HaNasi -- תניא, רבי אומר (63a.15-17)
the R' Yoshiya R' Tavi quotes, as in berakhot_15b
narrator of the Chanina story (הוה משתעי)
Chanina, son of R' Yehoshua's brother, who intercalated years in the exile
R' Yosei ben Kippar and the grandson of Zecharya ben Kevutal, sent after Chanina (63a.24)
the Sages of the Land who sent the two scholars (והם שיגרונו אצלך, 63a.27); speak through them

props.gloss_en: a person should never multiply friends in his house
as it is said: 'a man of friends is to be broken' (Prov 18:24)
a person should not appoint an administrator (apotropos) in his house
for had Potiphar not appointed Joseph administrator in his house, he would not have come to that matter
the nazir passage is juxtaposed to the sota passage to tell you that whoever sees a sota in her disgrace should abstain from wine
the sota passage is juxtaposed to terumot and tithes to tell you: whoever has terumot and tithes and does not give them to the priest will in the end need the priest through his wife
as it is said: 'and every man's holy things shall be his' (Num 5:10), and beside it 'any man whose wife goes astray' (5:12), and it is written 'the man shall bring his wife [to the priest]' (5:15)
and not only that, but in the end he will need them
as it is said: 'and every man's holy things shall be his' (Num 5:10)
and if he gave them, in the end he grows rich
as it is said: 'what any man gives the priest, it shall be his' (Num 5:10)
'it shall be his' -- much money
whoever joins the Name of Heaven to his distress, his livelihood is doubled for him
as it is said: 'and the Almighty shall be in your distress, and silver toafot to you' (Job 22:25)
his livelihood flies to him like a bird
as it is said: 'and silver toafot to you'
whoever slackens from words of Torah has no strength to stand on a day of distress
as it is said: 'if you slacken on the day of distress, your strength is narrow' (Prov 24:10)
and even [one who slackens from] a single mitzva
as it is said 'if you slacken' -- in any case [unqualified]
when Chanina, son of R' Yehoshua's brother, went down to the exile, he would intercalate years and fix months outside the Land
two scholars are sent after him; he asks: why have you come? they: we have come to learn Torah
he proclaimed about them: these men are the great of the generation, and their fathers served in the Temple
Zecharya ben Kevutal says: many times I read before him from the book of Daniel
he began to declare impure and they declared pure; he forbade and they permitted
he proclaimed about them: these men are worthless, they are nothing
you have already built and cannot tear down; you have already fenced and cannot breach
asked why they rule pure where he rules impure and permit where he forbids, they answer: because you intercalate years and fix months outside the Land
did not Akiva ben Yosef intercalate years and fix months outside the Land?
I too left none like me in the Land of Israel
go and tell him in our name: if he obeys, good; if not, let him be under a ban

and tell our brothers in the exile: if they obey, good; if not, let them go up a mountain, Achiya build an altar, Chananya play the harp, and let them all deny and say they have no portion in the God of Israel
at once all the people burst into weeping and said: God forbid, we have a portion in the God of Israel
and why all this? because it is said: 'for from Zion goes forth Torah and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem' (Isa 2:3)
a sage who declared impure -- his colleague may not declare pure; who forbade -- his colleague may not permit
